chapter: Theater broadcasts, recordings and the road
title: Drummers Raymond Baduc and Monk Hazel; talk about the tape
summary: He discusses Raymond Baduc subbing at Cobb's, the drummer Monk Hazel, and then the tape-recording arrangements.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Raymond used to sub, if my brother had a late show, I was making so much money I quit the office. It wasn't interesting anymore. You know I'm a leader. Because I had an outfit in Morrison's cafeteria. He used to have music there. I have outfits all over. And so if the off you had a late show, Raymond was playing at some cheap joint on Bourbon Street but he'd take his intermission at that time so he could rush in and open them with us at Cobb's. And my brother would give him a couple of dollars. And he was supposed to be one of the greatest sticks of my drummers. I couldn't see him. Because he used to juggle the sticks too much. My brother was down, you know. That Moncais style. That's another good drummer.

I used him, I couldn't keep him because he drank too much. I had to have respectable, he had no teeth. Well you're going to have some tape recording there. Well everybody would sell that. Well I want to tell you, it's a big deal.
Monk would sell that himself. Let me get you a bit.
